actions.justification: Mandatory first step to establish chief complaint, symptom timeline, cardiac history, medications, and risk factors relevant to suspected heart failure presentation.
Mandatory physical exam to assess for signs of heart failure (JVD, S3 gallop, pulmonary crackles, peripheral edema) and hemodynamic status.
Mandatory ECG to evaluate for arrhythmias, ischemia, LVH, or conduction abnormalities that may underlie or exacerbate heart failure.
Mandatory lab to assess renal function, electrolytes, and glucose, critical for heart failure workup and guiding treatment.
Mandatory biomarker to confirm heart failure diagnosis and assess severity of cardiac stress.
Mandatory lab to evaluate for anemia or infection contributing to cardiac decompensation.

Mandatory action - chest X-ray is essential to assess for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and pleural effusions in the workup of suspected heart failure. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Mandatory action - TSH is required to evaluate for thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause of heart failure. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.

Assessing hemodynamic profile (wet/dry, warm/cold) guides management decisions including diuretic therapy and vasodilator use, and is a key next step in heart failure evaluation after initial diagnostics are ordered.

Assessing left ventricular ejection fraction is a critical next step in heart failure workup to guide therapy selection (ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i, ARNI) and determine candidacy for device therapy (ICD/CRT).
After determining LVEF, assess ICD indication per guideline — patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤35%) may qualify for primary prevention ICD after optimizing GDMT for at least 3 months.
Assess CRT indication based on LVEF, QRS duration/morphology (LBBB), and NYHA functional class per guideline to determine if cardiac resynchronization therapy is appropriate.
NYHA functional classification is essential for guiding heart failure management, including medication titration and determining candidacy for advanced therapies. This has not yet been completed.
Assessing structural abnormalities (e.g., valvular disease, wall motion abnormalities) helps guide etiology-specific treatment and has not been completed yet.

Evaluating whether the patient is a candidate for advanced heart failure therapies (e.g., LVAD, transplant) is an important step in comprehensive heart failure workup, especially once LVEF and hemodynamic profile have been assessed.

Patient has been assessed for LVEF, NYHA class, ICD/CRT indication, and structural abnormalities. Next step is to evaluate whether guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) duration and optimization has been achieved before considering advanced therapies or device upgrades.

Cardiac rehabilitation is indicated for heart failure patients with stable hemodynamics (BP 120/80, HR 80, SpO2 98%) to improve functional capacity and outcomes as part of comprehensive HF management.
With HR of 80 bpm, assess if ivabradine is indicated (typically for HR ≥70 bpm in sinus rhythm on maximally tolerated beta-blocker with reduced EF) as part of GDMT optimization.

After comprehensive assessment of LVEF, NYHA class, ICD/CRT indication, and advanced therapy candidacy, confirming optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is the next priority to ensure the patient is on appropriate neurohormonal blockade and other evidence-based treatments for heart failure.
ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) is a cornerstone of GDMT for HFrEF, reducing mortality and hospitalizations. Should be initiated or optimized if not already at target dose.

Beta-blocker therapy (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol) is a mandatory component of GDMT for HFrEF with proven mortality benefit. Should be confirmed, initiated, or uptitrated as appropriate given stable hemodynamics (HR 80, BP 120/80).
MRA (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is a key GDMT component for HFrEF with EF ≤35% that reduces mortality and hospitalizations. Should be considered as part of optimizing medical therapy.
Candidacy for advanced therapies was already assessed; initiating comprehensive transplant workup is the logical next step for patients with advanced HF who may benefit from transplantation or MCS.
If volume overload or congestion is present in this HF patient, appropriate diuretic therapy should be optimized to relieve symptoms and reduce filling pressures.
